raw_response:
I am 63 years old and I have farmed these 8 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I only finished primary school, but I know this land better than any book. My household is me and my husband — two people — and we do most of the work ourselves, though at harvest we hire the combine. I grow wheat in winter and maize in summer on the same 8 mu, same as everyone around here.

The wheat is already in the ground from last October. I rotary tilled before sowing and planted Jimai 22, the improved variety. I have used it for years because my neighbors get steady yield with it and the seed is not too expensive. For fertilizer, I put down two bags — 100 kg — of 18-22-5 compound fertilizer per mu as base fertilizer. Then in spring when the wheat turns green, I spread 40 kg of urea per mu, and if the heads look thin I add another 20 kg at heading time. All together that comes to about 35 kg of nitrogen and 22 kg of phosphorus per mu. I do not buy extra potash; what is in the compound is enough, about 8 kg per mu. I know this is on the high side, but my neighbor Lao Wang uses the same amount and his wheat is always greener than mine. I would rather waste some fertilizer than risk empty heads. A bad harvest is a disaster; a few extra jin of fertilizer is just a cost. I irrigate three times from the well: once after sowing, once at jointing in March or April, and once at grain filling. Diesel for the pump costs real money, but three times is what everyone does here and I cannot risk drought. For spraying, I go out four times total — herbicide once after sowing, insecticide once in spring for aphids, and fungicide once if the weather turns damp. Last year I got about 1000 kg per mu and I expect the same this year if the weather holds.

After we harvest wheat in early June, I plant Denghai 605 hybrid maize the same day or the next day. Everyone here uses Denghai 605 now. The seed dealer says it gives the best yield and I have seen it work on my own field. I do not plow for maize — no-tillage, just plant straight into the wheat stubble. I put down about 80 kg per mu of 28-6-6 compound fertilizer at planting. The dealer sells it in 50 kg bags, so that is one and a half bags per mu. That gives about 22 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. Some people add extra urea at the big trumpet stage, but I find the compound is enough if the season is normal. I irrigate twice: once when the seedlings are small if it is dry, and once at the big trumpet stage. I spray three times total — herbicide once before the plants get too tall, and insecticide once or twice for corn borer. I expect about 1100 kg per mu. Last year was about that and I see no reason to change.

Every jin of fertilizer and every liter of diesel costs real money. I think about the whole year's spending because there are only two of us and 8 mu is not small. But I have learned over 40 years that cutting back too much is gambling with my income. I start from what worked last year, I watch what my neighbors buy at the dealer, and I adjust a little if I have to. If everyone is buying more urea this spring, I will buy more too.
